A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NAG/DL4ND research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original RotatedMNIST experiments, VLCS and CHAMMI-CP comparisons, synthetic-noise experiments, and analyses of sample selection and manually identified label noise.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds PACS and DomainNet evaluations, symmetric-noise experiments, component ablations, relabeling-precision measurements and warmup sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The warmup, GMM separation and low-loss proxy pipeline remains. However, v1 Section 4.2 selects the class with minimum average distance across other domains, whereas v2 Section 4.1 and Equation (3) select the nearest individual other-domain class proxy. This is a localized change to the procedure as specified; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The existing RotatedMNIST, VLCS, CHAMMI-CP, OfficeHome and TerraIncognita coverage remains. v2 adds real-noise PACS and synthetic-noise DomainNet evaluations, plus a symmetric-noise OfficeHome scenario beyond the earlier asymmetric corruption experiments. These substantially broaden the represented domains and noise conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAGM+SWAD+UNICON comparisons with and without per-domain sampling on VLCS and CHAMMI-CP (Tables 7, 9 and 10). The corresponding MIRO-based combinations and original standalone baselines remain. Newly discussed noisy-domain-adaptation methods are not directly benchmarked.

E3.justification: The leave-one-domain-out ID/OOD accuracy framework, retained backbones, batch size and stated VLCS/CHAMMI-CP training budget remain. Added experiments introduce a 20% TerraIncognita corruption condition, relabeling precision, component-removal controls and explicit warmup sweeps (Tables 4–6 and 12–13). These extend the evaluation design without replacing its basic protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct tests of relabeling versus discarding samples, cross-domain versus within-domain comparisons, and low-loss versus all-sample proxies (Table 5). Table 6 measures relabeling precision, and Tables 12–13 test warmup sensitivity. These substantially strengthen mechanism and robustness analyses. The earlier support-vector analysis and sample-selection tradeoff remain; v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or run-to-run variability for its performance results. The retained feature-distance boxplots describe sample distributions rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial benchmark, ablation, precision and sensitivity results. For example, Table 4 reports DomainNet OOD accuracy of 35.6 for SAGM+DL4ND versus 26.9 for SAGM in the newly evaluated setting. Most retained scores match after rounding, but the CHAMMI-CP ERM average is corrected from 58.18 in v1 Table 2 to 59.8 in v2 Table 8.

T1.justification: v1 introduces a sample-to-class versus sample-to-domain distance assumption and claims cross-domain separability as Theorem 1. v2 removes that theorem and its expectation-based formulation, replacing the earlier assumption with a class-domain-proxy distance-ordering condition in Equation (2), assessed empirically. This substantially revises the formal justification rather than merely changing notation.

C1.justification: The joint ID-noise/OOD-generalization objective and cross-domain DL4ND contribution remain central. v2 broadens the headline validation claim to seven datasets and three noise types and explicitly describes DL4ND as the first direct NAG method. These extend the claimed scope without replacing the paper's central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix C interprets VLCS noise mainly as missing annotations for co-occurring categories, whereas v1 Section 3.3 describes labels that do not match image content. v2 also qualifies v1's favorable interpretation of regularization combinations by attributing ELR+DG underperformance to excessive constraints. New discussion addresses erroneous relabeling of difficult domains, validation-based warmup selection, and multimodal-model applicability and contamination concerns.

D1.justification: v1 mentions an accompanying code archive and promises later public release; v2 supplies a project-code link and states that code, data and pretrained models are released. It adds DomainNet corruption mappings and warmup-selection guidance. Conversely, explicit disclosures about cleaning VLCS test sets and modifying the five-channel input layer disappear. Existing hardware details and six integration algorithms are retained.

R1.justification: v1 primarily surveys DG and LNL separately. v2 Section 2 and the new Appendix B substantially position NAG against noisy domain adaptation, discussing works including Shu et al., Han et al. and Yin et al. Additional recent pretraining and multimodal-model literature supports new positioning around benchmark contamination and backbone choice.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, challenge analysis, method exposition and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 adopts question-led subsections, real-world dataset discussion moves into Appendix C, and the appendices are reorganized into extended results, domain-adaptation comparisons, noise information and implementation details.

P2.justification: The two-column manuscript becomes a single-column conference layout, with redrawn conceptual illustrations and extensively reorganized displays. v1 Table 2 is redistributed across v2 Tables 8–10 and summarized by the new Figure 6 scatterplots. Existing figures move to the appendices, while new benchmark, ablation, precision and sensitivity tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's benchmark comparisons and toy analysis did not directly isolate the proposed components on its main datasets. v2 Tables 5–6 address that important deficiency through component ablations and relabeling-precision tests, while Tables 12–13 examine warmup sensitivity. Broader dataset and noise coverage further strengthens empirical support. These gains outweigh documentation regressions, notably the unexplained averaging-versus-nearest-proxy discrepancy and omission of VLCS test-cleaning details. Run-to-run uncertainty remains unreported.
